t_advice_summary_textbox.text: The last player noticed that the main variables between the gnomes are hat length and colour. They also said that there are 4 rounds of play. They said that during the first 3 rounds the long hats tend to give more mushrooms/points than the short hats. They said that pink tends to score higher than blue and that green scores higher than orange. However, in the 4th round it seemed that the opposite was true; the orange hats score higher than green and the blue hats score higher than pink. They weren't so sure on how hat length was affecting the scores but suggested switching to choosing the gnome with a shorter hat if you notice that the long hat is no longer scoring well.

vb_textbox.text: Every round shows a pair of gnomes. The gnomes are always shown in the same pairing; a gnome with a green hat is paired with a gnome with an orange hat, a gnome with a small yellow hat is paired with a gnome with a long purple hat, a gnome with a small red hat is paired with a gnome with a long brown hat, a gnome with a pink hat is paired with a gnome with a blue hat. The pairs of gnomes are never altered. I advise using the 'lower risk' rounds where there is (x1) points to be gained to 'test' which gnome of each pair is paying the highest reward. Then try to continue selecting the higher paying gnome going forward. At times it feels like there is a 'switch' between which gnome is paying more. Again, I advise using the (x1) rounds to test that theory when you can - so that you don't miss out on points paying (x5).
